predecessors.name: Later Tang
predecessors.text: the Later Tang realm, which Shi Jingtang took after Li Congke's fall on 11 January 937 (Later Tang infobox)

successors.name: Later Han (Five Dynasties)
successors.text: the Later Han realm, Liu Zhiyuan's state proclaimed in 947

successors.name: Liao dynasty (Great Khitan State)
successors.text: Kaifeng and the Hebei plain, taken by the Khitan in January 947

ledger.x: 936: Shi Jingtang is proclaimed emperor of the Later Jin, with Khitan help.
28 November 936: the Later Jin is founded as a Liao client.
937: the Later Tang heartland comes over after Li Congke's fall.
937: the capital moves from Taiyuan to Luoyang.
937: the capital moves on to Kaifeng.
938: the Sixteen Prefectures pass to the Khitan.
Summer 942: Shi Chonggui breaks the subordination.
944: the Liao invade the Hebei plain.
947: the Liao take the Later Jin realm.

wars.name: Shi Jingtang's revolt against Later Tang
wars.outcome: Shi Jingtang overthrew Li Congke (Later Tang ended 11 January 937) with Khitan aid and gave the Liao the Sixteen Prefectures and annual tribute.

wars.name: Liao-Later Jin war
wars.outcome: Liao victory: the army at Zhongdu Bridge surrendered in 946 and Kaifeng fell on 11 January 947; Shi Chonggui was exiled to Huanglong; the Liao withdrew within the year.

wars.name: An Congjin's rebellion
wars.outcome: Crushed: An Congjin rebelled after Shi Jingtang left Kaifeng and later committed suicide; no border moved.

wars.name: Fan Yanguang's revolt
wars.outcome: Crushed by siege: Fan's army was beaten at the Yellow River crossing in 937, Yedu was besieged to fall 938 and Fan surrendered; Zhang Congbin, who joined him and took Heyang and Luoyang, was beaten too.

certainty.note: No treaty line on any opened page.
The suzerainty has ended and the war of 944-947 moves the front over the Hebei plain; no line is on any page.
